texts: good. the date comes through as separate day-47 and year-1 terms on the moon's full state, and the plain "the moon was full" fact is kept beside the dated state so either question resolves.
good. the convening, the Council as the one convening, and the Watch as the place all come through, and the Council symbol here is the one every later sentence reuses.

good. the report reaches the Council with Sailsworn as the reporter, and the reported claim — the salt-bloom store holding fourteen weeks of winter supply — is kept whole as the report's content, with the store typed as a kind of store at top level.
good. issuer, recipient station and the ration itself all come through, the ration typed as a winter feather ration (and so a ration) and marked standard.

mixed: the reporting, Bevin Coombe, the Council and the Stilllight Lantern are all recorded, but the content of the report is dropped entirely — a reported clause that is nothing but a denial ("no wraith had approached...") has no form the translator can carry inside a report, so the parse leaves a report with nothing reported. State the same news positively so it survives inside the report: "Bevin Coombe reported to the Council that the Stilllight Lantern had remained free of wraiths."
good. same shape as the Sailsworn report — reporter, Council and the sealed claim about the feather store holding eight weeks of supply, with the store typed at top level.

bad: "for the coming month" is read as WHEN the Council issued the feathers, which contradicts day 47 of Year 1 — the parse asserts the issuing happened next month — and it anchors to a month this world's day-of-year calendar never names; separately, "extra" ends up asserted of every individual feather rather than of the amount. Give the coverage period its own clause as a plain span and say what the feathers are extra to: "In addition to the standard ration, the Council issued ground feathers to the Stilllight Station, and those feathers supplied the station for one month."

bad: the same two faults as the previous sentence (the coverage period taken as the issuing's own time, contradicting day 47; "extra" predicated of each feather), plus a third: "nearest the Sunken Cove" is weakened to merely "near the Sunken Cove", because a superlative measured against a landmark has no form the translator can carry — so which two stations were meant is lost. Identify the two stations by name rather than by proximity, and split the period off as before: "In addition to their standard rations, the Council issued ground feathers to the [first station's name] and the [second station's name], and those feathers supplied both stations for one month."
